newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain doubts labour reform radical enough.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain doubts labour reform radical enough.

text.p: The Bank of Spain doubts that the reform of the labour market currently under discussion by trade unions and employers will be radical enough, the board member Julio Segura said on Friday.
Segura said he expects the two parts will reach an agreement.

"It's very likely that they'll make a deal, but I'm not sure that the agreement will be radical enough as a reform of the labour market," Segura said at an economic summit in the Spanish sea-side town of Sitges.
Segura downplayed new contracts that employers and trade unions are discussing, saying that they are not new.
He said Spain's job market currently has three problems: high costs of dismissals, the collective agreement framework, and high level of unemployment benefits.
On firing costs, Segura said this point was highly affected by courts in deciding fair dimissals causes.
"It does not seem the agreement will settle this point," he said. --Madrid Newsroom +34 1 585 2167
